- My aim was achieved: the top-performing cluster (M11, M14, M15, M16, M18, M20) is now clearly separated and shares a common mechanistic theme—deactivation driven by the substrate or the catalyst-substrate complex (catS).

<hypothesis>
To distinguish between the remaining top models (M11, M14, M16, M18, M20), we must probe the kinetic order of the deactivation process with respect to the substrate and the catS complex. By using a maximum, saturating substrate concentration (S = 5.0) and a moderate catalyst concentration (cat = 0.1), we will drive almost all the catalyst into the bound catS state. 
Under these conditions:
1. M14 (first-order catS deactivation) will exhibit a saturated, constant deactivation rate.
2. M16 (substrate-induced catS deactivation) will show a drastically accelerated deactivation rate, as its rate depends on both [catS] and free [S], which remains high.
3. M11 (substrate-induced deactivation of free cat) and M20 (deactivation of free cat) will be heavily suppressed because the pool of free catalyst is depleted.
4. M18 (second-order catS deactivation) will scale differently than the first-order models.
This extreme saturation regime will cleanly separate M14 (S-independent at saturation) from M16 (S-dependent at saturation) while simultaneously testing the free-catalyst deactivation models.
</hypothesis>
